team: Full Derek Mcinnes Press Conference after
quote_text:
"You must be very proud of your boys’  efforts to get through that game." 
Yeah, it wasn’t just the effort.  The effort was ridiculously good.  
Anytime you do get down to 10 men,  it’s not just your own performance;  
you need to make sure you give it  a performance and a half, really.
We had to play the game a certain way. We had  to stay within the shape, we had to make loads  
of decisions. It’s my job to try and give  ourselves the best chance to win a game,  
and obviously, after Bruce scores and gets us  in front, it gives us something to hold on to.
But it was becoming clear to me, too often, we  were having two center-forwards at the edge of  
our box having to clear things at the end of the  first half. And it was becoming clear because  
they were coming from behind us. We needed  to make sure we had a flat midfield three.
It’s my job to try and give everybody the best  chance to win. But wow, the boys were magnificent.  
And to do it for so long, we’ve had to work too  hard too often this season because of red cards.  
But, you know, only positives for me from that.
You know, Bruce, we had to  sacrifice him at halftime,  
but he’s away as a match-winner again.  He’s up to five goals, he’s looking sharp.  
No player likes to come off, but he, once  again, he’s dependable and gets his goal.
But behind it all was a brilliant effort,  
I thought, from the subs as well—coming on  and getting to the pace of the game. But  
so many decisions had to be made—good  decisions—when you’re down to 10 men.
And I know Oda hits the bar at the  end, and he’s got that quality,  
and he should be running on a body there.  And part of the reason we were playing  
three flat midfielders was for that type  of scenario, with boys coming on as well,  
and Spitt’s ability and Deas’ ability. And  it was probably the one time that he had  
a wee sight of our goal. That would’ve been so  harsh on us if that had gone in. But we deserved  
a wee bit of luck. There’s no doubt about it.  I know everybody says that, and everybody’s  
so partisan for their own club, but Christ,  Kilmarnock deserved a wee bit of luck today.
And we had the best chances in the game.  We had more shots on target than them,  
even with 10 men. We countered brilliantly,  
had some real good moments. So it was  almost a complete performance with 10 men.
Not that you would set up this way, but sometimes  you do scenarios when you’re down to 10 men in  
training, and you maybe do it for 20  minutes, half an hour, and it’s really  
just to plant the seed of decision-making  and picking and choosing your fights.
But to do it for 90 minutes—it was a  monumental effort. Some three points are  
better than others, and that feels like  a brilliant three points for us today.
"On Robbie Deas’ red card:" See, at the time, I actually wasn’t  
sure it was even a yellow. But I thought  Don Robertson, standing right next to it,  
he’s seen it for what it is and looked  at it as a yellow card. Right away,  
I’m thinking, "Here we go. We need to be careful."
When it actually was announced it was  going to VAR, you always fear the worst,  
clearly. And when I’ve seen it back  now, I can see why that would’ve  
looked pretty nasty on VAR. So I’m not  saying it’s not the right decision.
It certainly wasn’t what Don Robertson  indicated as scissors. But he has come down,  
his right foot on Vargas, and if you freeze it,  
it doesn’t look great on his ankle. I think  Deas, in his defense, has kind of slipped  
at the last wee bit and lost his footing. I  don’t think he’s coming at any real speed.
But listen, this is the thing about this  inconsistency. I was here a few weeks ago, and I  
watched it firsthand. I wasn’t sure it was a red.  But when I watched that, and it went, I don’t  
know how, for the life of me, it didn’t. I knew it  wouldn’t have looked great on VAR, and it didn’t.
This is the thing—the inconsistency is  awful at the minute. It is. There’s a  
Hearts player out there—I’m not going  to name him—he was eventually booked,  
but he should’ve been booked twice  before he actually gets booked.
And he wasn’t booked for offenses  that my players have been booked  
for over the last few games, which  ultimately ended up with red cards.
So, it shouldn't be the same offense  and one thing I'll keep banging on  
about. All football managers are  the same. But the inconsistency.  
The same offense should be a yellow, or  it’s not a yellow for the same offense.
It shouldn’t dependent on which referee you  get. There has to be a clearer direction,  
and we’re not getting it. But I’m not moaning. I’m  not moaning because we won. I’m buzzing. Buzzing.
"On Sam Walker coming off at halftime:" Yeah, obviously, he got a bang last week  
at Tannadice. We had restricted  his kicking this week, really,  
just for the last couple of days. But he got a  clean bill of health yesterday to be in the goal.
But it was clear to me after the very first kick,  
he was struggling. And a lot of his kicks  were actually putting us under pressure. He  
wasn’t getting any real distance,  wasn’t getting any real accuracy.
So the decision was made. I  thought Kean Harrar was excellent.
title: Full Derek Mcinnes Press Conference after 1-0 victory over Hearts
